question: Among valid 1:4 daily matched opportunities that remain predominantly natural forest immediately before the index fire season, is a fire-positive cell more likely than its matched fire-negative cells to lose natural forest during the following one to three annual land-cover maps?

estimand.primary: Adjusted within-matched-set risk difference for losing at least 10% of pre-index natural-forest area by the one-year follow-up map, comparing the index-day fire-positive cell with four valid fire-negative cells.

exposure.positive: outcome_status == positive on the registered VNP14A1 event day
exposure.negative: outcome_status == negative and valid_opportunity == true on that same matched-set day
exposure.matched_set: one positive plus four reusable controls within 25 km on the same day
exposure.future_fire_policy: Retain controls that burn later; the estimand is index-day detection status, not permanent absence of fire. Repeated cells require cell-clustered uncertainty.

outcome_source.product: Collection 4.1 annual land cover and land use
outcome_source.license: CC BY-SA for public-interest/non-commercial use, subject to provider terms

time_alignment.no_2026_outcome_claim: Collection 4.1 ends in 2024; 2025 and 2026 land-cover outcomes are unavailable in this product as of registration.

primary_binary.definition: fraction of the cell that was natural forest in event_year-1 and is non-natural-forest at event_year+1, divided by pre-index natural-forest fraction, is at least 0.10

outcomes.destination_interpretation: Destination classes are descriptive transitions only. Oil-palm classification is not actor, intent, ownership, legality, or profit attribution.

model.uncertainty: two-way cluster-robust covariance by cell and index date; cell-only fallback must be disclosed if two-way covariance is invalid
model.secondary_family_correction: Holm within the named horizon and destination families

mandatory_reporting: matched sets and rows at every exclusion step
mean, median, SD, p25, and p75 outcome distributions by index-day exposure
adjusted risk difference with 95% confidence interval and two-sided p-value
unadjusted matched risks and risk ratio with zero-cell handling disclosed
hard_claim_boundaries: A subsequent oil-palm class does not show that the fire was deliberately set to create a plantation.
The analysis cannot identify an individual, company, concession holder, or beneficiary.
The analysis cannot measure government mitigation, enforcement, restoration, or negligence without dated intervention data.
Kalimantan results do not establish a global pattern; Phase 5 requires harmonized replication.
